tips.text: To decide a call, compare your equity with the price: you need at least call ÷ (pot + bet + call). A half-pot bet needs 25%, a pot-sized bet 33%.

tips.text: Quick estimate for your draw: multiply your outs by 4 with two cards to come, by 2 with one card to come. It's within a point or two up to about nine outs and overstates big draws.

tips.text: In Omaha, drawing to a flush that isn't the nut flush is a classic beginner leak: against several opponents a bigger flush is often out there, so many of your 'outs' lose.

tips.text: In Omaha the nuts on the flop is often only the temporary nuts: with two cards to come, a hand with no redraw can be overtaken. Having the nuts plus a draw to a better nuts is much stronger than the bare nuts.

tips.text: Pot-limit sizing: first count the pot as if you had called, then raise by that amount on top. Max raise to = largest bet + (pot including all bets + your call).
